The test image shows a soybean plant from below, focusing on the lower stem area near the soil line. I can see stems, some pods, and leaves with some browning/yellowing. There appears to be discoloration on the stems. This is a stem/whole_plant view.

Top candidates from stem/whole_plant categories: Phytophthora, White_Mold, Charcoal_Rot, Anthracnose, Rhizoctonia, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, Sudden_death_syndrome, Fusarium.

Let me view reference images one per class.
This Phytophthora stem reference is very similar to the test image - same angle, dark stem discoloration near soil line, mix of green and dying foliage. Let me check a few more candidates.

I've used all 8 reference views. The Phytophthora stem reference (Soybean_Dise_57.jpg) was the strongest match by far, showing nearly identical characteristics to the test image:

- Same viewing angle from ground level looking at lower stems
- Dark brown discoloration on stems extending from the soil line upward
- Mix of green and yellowing/dying leaves
- Pods still present on the plant
- Characteristic chocolate-brown stem coloring

This matches the Phytophthora symptom description: "dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward, yellowing and wilting leaves that stay attached." Other candidates (White_Mold, Charcoal_Rot, Anthracnose, Rhizoctonia, Fusarium, TSV, SDS) showed distinctly different visual presentations.
